Forecast scorecard unchanged from the 2026-08-01 ad-hoc review: 1 confirmed (revenue beat), 1 falsified (EBITDA beat -- the record was wrong, in the company's favor), 1 not assessable (receivables/DSO -- still no settling data found), 1 confirmed-on-direction-only (net debt rose, no comparable-basis multiple claimed), 2 still open (margin fade to Oct-2026; Alumetal impairment to Feb-2027). No new quarterly print landed in the three weeks since the ad-hoc review, so nothing new resolves.

A secondary web source (TipRanks) computed a 'net debt/EBITDA of ~2.56x' by dividing quarter-end net debt by a single quarter's adjusted EBITDA rather than trailing-twelve-month EBITDA -- a basis mismatch against the original 1.02x reading. That figure is explicitly rejected here rather than carried into the record (CLAUDE.md §15 matched-basis ratios); the net-debt forecast stays confirmed on direction only.

Qatalum is still running at ~60% of nameplate capacity a month on, with no restart timeline disclosed -- the operational risk is persisting, not resolving, which is itself informative for the 12-month horizon but does not move thesis_status.

Thesis status remains on-track: 33 days into a 12-month-horizon Watchlist call is still early, no kill criterion has triggered, and the single most decision-relevant unresolved item (does the Adjusted EBITDA margin fade toward ~13% or hold near 17%+) needs the 23-Oct-2026 print, not this one. decision_quality stays 'not assessable' on the same ground as the ad-hoc review -- a one-month return on a Watchlist/no-position call is not yet a scoreable outcome even though it is now benchmark-relative.

memo_delta.stage_one_comment: Nothing new landed at Norsk Hydro in the three weeks since our last update. The next quarterly print is not due until 23 October, so the two open questions from before are still open: whether the adjusted EBITDA margin fades back toward the mid-teens as aluminium prices soften, and whether the receivables spike from the first quarter ever gets explained. The shares are up about 3.9 percent since our 17 July reference price, but that trails the broader Oslo market, which rose about 5.3 percent over the same stretch, while beating the aluminium price itself, which was up less than 1 percent. Qatalum, the Qatari smelter running at reduced output since a gas-supply disruption in March, is still stuck at about 60 percent of capacity with no restart date given. None of this changes the call. We remain on the watchlist with no new position, waiting on the October print and on price falling toward our fair-value band before revisiting.
